faq.q: Why do I get butterflies in my tummy?
faq.a: When you are nervous, your body gets ready for action and sends blood away from your tummy to your muscles. That change can feel like fluttering butterflies. It fades as you calm down.
asks: What are butterflies in your stomach?
Why does my tummy feel funny when I am nervous?

faq.q: Why does my face get hot when I am angry?
faq.a: Anger makes tiny blood vessels in your face open wider, so more warm blood flows near your skin. That is why your face can feel hot and look red.
asks: Why do I go red when I am cross?

faq.q: Why do I get a lump in my throat when I am sad?
faq.a: When you are sad, and especially when you try not to cry, small muscles in your throat tighten. That feels like a lump. It goes away as the feeling passes.
asks: What is the lump in my throat when I want to cry?

faq.q: Why does my heart beat fast when I am scared?
faq.a: Your brain's alarm tells your body to get ready to move. Your heart pumps faster to send extra blood and oxygen to your muscles.
asks: Why does my heart pound when I am frightened?

faq.q: Can a feeling make my tummy really hurt?
faq.a: Yes, worry can cause a real tummy ache. If it happens a lot, tell a grown-up you trust, and they may take you to a doctor to check you are okay.
asks: Can worry make you feel sick?

facts: In a 2014 study from Finland, more than 700 people coloured where they felt emotions on a body map, and people from different countries drew very similar maps.
When you are scared, your adrenal glands release adrenaline, which makes your heart beat faster.
